dedupe_keys.name: sharedstreets trip simulator synthetic gps telemetry for cars bikes and scooters

description: trip-simulator is a tool from SharedStreets that generates simulated raw GPS telemetry, created because real GPS traces are sensitive and easy to de-anonymise. Coverage: any area with OpenStreetMap data; the README shows one million trips simulated over New York City. It is a multi-agent model for cars, bikes or scooters that needs no inputs besides an OpenStreetMap extract, generates pickups and drop-offs from network density, and adds physically realistic GPS noise so that telemetry algorithms can be tested. Format and access: a Node.js command-line tool installed with npm, taking an OSM PBF file and a vehicle configuration, and writing 1 Hz location probes plus trips and status changes that comply with the Mobility Data Specification (MDS). Licence and cost: MIT, free. Caveats: synthetic demand is not calibrated to observed travel; maintenance status was not checked. It supports agent-based testing of data pipelines and operational tools for shared mobility fleets without using personal data. It relates to the Mobility Data Specification and OpenStreetMap in the catalogue.
